content:
Maria: Heads-up — saw multiple GPU nodes scaled down overnight and pods sat Pending for >6m while CA spun up new nodes. Logs show CA chose them as "scale-down candidates: 3 nodes" then removed them.
Sam: Which flags are we running for CA in prod-gpu pool?
Maria: Using: --expander=least-waste --scale-down-unneeded-time=10m --scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.5 --skip-nodes-with-local-storage=true
Cheng: least-waste is binpacking-friendly, but with GPUs it can evict smaller pods and drain entire nodes. For GPU pools we usually want --expander=most-pods or explicit node group weights.
Anya: Also saw many pods have high 'preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution' affinity so they don't reschedule nicely.
Luke: Suggest bumping --scale-down-unneeded-time to 20m and add --scale-down-delay-after-add=15m for GPU nodegroups. Prevents churn during bursts.
OpsBot: [alert] cluster-autoscaler: scaleDown: removing node "gpunode-05" (utilization 8%)
Sam: We also rely on PodDisruptionBudgets for model servers; CA considers PDBs and will avoid evicting, but some of ours have maxUnavailable: 100% (oops).
Maria: Oof. Fix: set PDB minAvailable=1 for critical model servers, or mark model servers with nodeSelector to stable pool.
Cheng: Another idea: set node group priority and weights in cloud provider autoscaler annotations so CA prefers draining cheaper spot pools first.
Anya: For k8s config, also enable --balance-similar-node-groups=false? or true? Thoughts.
Sam: balance-similar-node-groups=true can help but it needs similar nodegroups. Our GPU types differ between region-a (A100) and region-b (A10). Might confuse CA.
Luke: For fragmentation, consider packing multiple small inference containers per GPU with MIG or device-plugin. But that's longer-term.
Maria: Quick actionable: change flags for gpu nodegroups to:
```bash
--scale-down-unneeded-time=20m
--scale-down-delay-after-add=15m
--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.6
--expander=most-pods
--max-empty-bulk-delete=1
```
Cheng: Also set --skip-nodes-with-system-pods=false? No, keep true to avoid deleting nodes with critical daemonsets.
Anya: We should also annotate stateful GPU nodegroups with capacityReservation=true and use reserved pools for steady traffic; cheaper than repeated scale up.
Sam: Cost note: keeping 1 reserved GPU per region ~ $X/month but cuts 6m cold start and reduces scale events.
Maria: I'll open a PR to change flags for prod-gpu-ASG and add PDB fixes. Assigning to @Cheng for reviewing.
Cheng: I'll review. Let's also add a small runbook for when CA evicts model-serving pods:
```bash
# quick triage
kubectl get pods -n models -o wide | grep Pending
kubectl describe pod <pending-pod>
kubectl get pdb -n models
# if node was removed, check CA logs
kubectl -n kube-system logs deploy/cluster-autoscaler | tail -n 200
# emergency: cordon and drain safe node, or scale up fallback group
kubectl cordon <node>
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```
OpsBot: [deploy] Updated cluster-autoscaler configmap in staging.
Luke: I'll run a 48h staging soak with the new flags and report numbers.
Maria: thanks :thumbsup:
